question:
Case Study:

Let $A = \{1,2,3\}$ and $B = \{a,b,c\}$. Consider all possible relations from $A$ to $B$.

(a) How many possible relations are there from $A$ to $B$?

(b) Define a function $f: A \to B$ by $f(1)=a$, $f(2)=b$, $f(3)=c$. Is $f$ invertible? Provide justification.

(c) List all possible number of functions $f : A \to B$ that are one-to-one.
explanation:
(a) The total number of relations from $A$ to $B$ is $2^{|A|\times|B|} = 2^{3\times3} = 512$.

(b) $f$ is a function assigning each element of $A$ to a unique element in $B$, i.e., it is a bijection. Therefore, $f$ is invertible.

(c) The number of one-to-one functions from $A$ to $B$ (when $|A|=|B|$): $3! = 6$.

options.A:
(a) $2^3=8$ relations.
(b) $f$ is not invertible.
(c) Number of one-to-one functions is $3$.
options.B:
(a) $3^3=27$ relations.
(b) $f$ is invertible because it is onto only.
(c) Number of one-to-one functions is $9$.
options.C:
(a) $3! = 6$ relations.
(b) $f$ is not invertible because $A\ne B$ as sets.
(c) Number of one-to-one functions is $512$.
options.D:
(a) $2^{3\times3}=512$ relations.
(b) $f$ is invertible because it is a bijection from $A$ to $B$.
(c) Number of one-to-one functions from $A$ to $B$ is $3!=6$.
